analyzed_vuln.description: `get_buffer` allocates the persistent edge-emulation scratch buffer as `pic->f->linesize[0] * 17` bytes, implicitly assuming the luma stride is at least the maximum emulated block width. SVQ3 motion compensation can request a 17x17 luma block (`width + 1`, `height + 1` with a 16x16 partition). For a very narrow frame whose aligned luma stride is only 16 bytes, the buffer is 16*17 bytes but `ff_emulated_edge_mc_8` writes 17 bytes per row using that 16-byte stride; on the final row its right-edge fill writes at offset 17*16, one byte past the allocation (crash at videodsp_template.c:101). The scratch allocation must independently guarantee both the required row width and row count rather than deriving total size solely from a possibly-too-small frame stride.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The input/harness must initialize the SVQ3 decoder with a sufficiently narrow valid frame size so the custom frame allocator produces luma `linesize[0] == 16`, then provide a decodable inter-predicted macroblock with an out-of-frame motion vector. `svq3_mc_dir_part` enters edge emulation and requests a 17x17 luma block into `s->edge_emu_buffer`; the 16-byte scratch stride causes overlapping rows and the right-edge byte of the seventeenth row is written immediately beyond the 272-byte allocation made by `get_buffer`.

args: Analyze the edge-emulation scratch-buffer sizing and stride usage in `svq3_mc_dir_part()` and `get_buffer()` in `ffmpeg/libavcodec/svq3.c`. What are the maximum luma and chroma emulated block dimensions, what stride is passed to `emulated_edge_mc`, and what minimal root-cause patch safely handles a luma frame linesize smaller than 17? Consider whether allocation can persist across resolution/stride changes and whether changing only allocation size is sufficient if the scratch stride remains the frame linesize.

ASan reports a one-byte heap overflow in ff_emulated_edge_mc_8 called from svq3_mc_dir_part. get_buffer currently allocates edge_emu_buffer with av_calloc(pic->f->linesize[0], 17). A narrow valid frame can have luma linesize 16, while luma MC requests width+1 and height+1 for a 16x16 partition, hence 17x17. The edge helper writes rows using the destination stride supplied by svq3_mc_dir_part, reportedly linesize[0]. I need a root-cause C patch, not an input filter, preserving normal decoding.

Explain the exact allocation expression needed, including whether 17 extra bytes, 17*17, or FFMAX(stride,17)*17 is correct given ff_emulated_edge_mc_8's final write. Also inspect whether FFmpeg padding/SIMD requirements imply a larger constant allocation.

I tried `av_calloc(FFMAX(pic->f->linesize[0], 17), 17)`, but validation still reports the same ff_emulated_edge_mc_8 dedup. I also tried a much more invasive fixed scratch stride plus temporary destination approach; validation still reported the same dedup, so I reverted all edits. Original code is restored. The known ASan address is exactly one byte after a 272-byte allocation (16*17), with 17x17 and buf stride 16. The task description emphasizes allocation sizing, not changing MC behavior. I need determine the intended robust C patch and account for why max(stride,17)*17 might still fail.
